newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks close mixed in thin pre-holiday trade.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks close mixed in thin pre-holiday trade.

text.p: Tokyo stocks closed mixed on Monday in extremely light trading as Sunday's Group of Seven (G7) meeting failed to provide fresh incentives to the stock market, and most participants were unwilling to move actively before a holiday tomorrow, brokers said.

The key 225-share Nikkei average closed up 57.51 points or 0.31 percent at 18,670.37, after hovering within a limited range throughout the session. June Nikkei futures gained 20 points to end at 18,650.
But the broader-based TOPIX index gave up 0.78 points or 0.06 percent to close at 1,410.85.
Its volume of a hefty 6.927 million shares was the heaviest. Taisei, a major general contractor, said on Friday that it would buy back up to 55 million of its own shares, worth up to 25 billion yen.
Toagosei Co Ltd, which announced a share buy-back earlier this year, rose 11 yen to 466, while Denso Corporation, which announced a buy-back last year, gained 50 yen to 2,760.
Late on Monday, major chemical firm Mitsubishi Chemical Corp said it plans to buy back up to 40 billion yen worth of its stock, or up to 100 million shares.
Brokerages lost ground, as worries about the industry lingered after Nomura Securities Co Ltd was hit by a scandal involving suspected illegal deals.
Nomura shares lost 20 yen to 1,370, while Yamaichi Securities Co Ltd shed 25 yen to 318, Daiwa Securities Co Ltd fell 27 yen to 818, and Nikko Securities Co Ltd eased 17 yen to 680.
The second section index inched down 1.39 points to 1,654.07, with 5.78 million shares traded. The over-the-counter (OTC) index was down 1.99 points at 1,134.56.
